Shared test vectors for the Turkish command parser (TekstilCAD.Core.Commands.CommandParser and any platform port). Hand-authored from tasarim/FINAL_COMMANDS.md, independent of the parser source.
FILE LAYOUT: top-level keys are _comment (this text), contexts and cases. Readers ignore the optional per-case key note.
CONTEXTS: maps a context name to the ordered list of current piece names. B0 = empty project, B1 = three pieces (Ön beden, Arka beden, Kol), B8 = two pieces (Ön beden, Ön beden 2). The spec contexts B2-B7 behave like B1 for the parser, so they are not listed.
CASE: every case has input (the raw text, JSON-escaped, may contain tabs, newlines, control characters), context (a key of contexts) and expect. expect is EITHER a refusal form OR a command form, never both (kind XOR refusal). Keys that do not belong to the chosen form or kind are forbidden.
REFUSAL FORM: {"refusal": "Rxx", optional "buttons": [strings], optional "fills": [strings]}. Codes are the strings R01..R28b from the spec, e.g. R15a, R15b, R16b. The R06 unit question uses this form too: refusal R06, buttons = the two texts that fill the input box, i.e. the typed text with ' mm' and ' cm' inserted right after the last number. R05 (ambiguous number such as 1.500) uses buttons = the typed text with the number replaced by the decimal reading (trailing zeros stripped) and the integer reading. R15b uses buttons = the matching piece names in project order. When buttons is absent the case does not check buttons.
COMMAND FORM: {"kind": K, fields}. Missing field or JSON null means not set. Numbers are millimetres, degrees or counts and are compared with tolerance 1e-9. Kinds and fields: Rect(width, height, optional square=true only for the word kare); Line(length, orientation horizontal|vertical); Move(right, down); MoveTo(x, y); Rotate(degrees 90|180|270, direction clockwise|counterclockwise); Mirror(axis: vertical = left-right flip, horizontal = top-bottom flip); Resize(width, height, JSON null for the unchanged side); Rename(name, case as typed); Delete(target selected|named, name only when named); Select(target named|next|previous|none, name only when named); Undo(steps 1..10); Redo; Help; CancelPreview; View(action fitAll|fitSelected|zoomIn|zoomOut|panLeft|panRight|panUp|panDown|detailedView|textLarger|textSmaller|themeDark|themeLight|allTools); Tool(tool select|line|polyline|rectangle|bezier|arc); FinishDrawing(action close|finishOpen|cancel|removeLastPoint); File(action save|saveAs|saveCopy|open|new); Handoff(target importDxf|export|exportSelectedDxf|exportSelectedA4|textileTools|machineCenter|grainline|pieceMetadata|mirrorCopy|groupMove|duplicate|layers|coordinateDrawing|about|designRequest|recoveryScan, optional tab int, optional value number).
OPTIONAL FLAGS: a command expect may carry unitAssumed (true = the command carries a length and no unit word was typed anywhere, so bare millimetres were assumed, including moves, positions, resize, seam and fabric-width values; false = a unit was typed or the command has no length). A refusal expect may carry incomplete (true = the text is a plausible prefix of a valid command, the refusal code still applies on Enter; false = a finished text that is simply refused). Both flags are asserted only when present in the case; the older cases of this file do not set them.
UNITS AND DIRECTIONS:lengths are millimetres. A bare number is mm; unit words mm/milim/milimetre, cm/santim/santimetre, m/metre; the last unit written applies to all bare numbers in the command; compound lengths add (1 santim 2 milim = 12 mm). Directions are screen directions: right is positive, down is positive, so up is NEGATIVE down (yarım santim yukarı = Move right 0, down -5). Select by name returns the typed name lower-cased with Turkish rules and without the accusative suffix (ön bedeni -> ön beden). Rename keeps the typed case. Ranges: 1..20000 mm for drawing, resize and move distances (R04 outside, zero is always R04); MoveTo positions may be 0..20000. The planner-level refusals (no selection, drawing in progress, locked layer, and so on) are NOT parser results: the parser still returns the command for them.
RULE FOR PORTS: a parser port must pass every case in this file, comparing kind and every listed field, or the refusal code and the listed buttons. The first 60 cases are the 60 test phrases of section 5 of the spec, in order (case index n-1 is phrase n); phrases whose context is B2..B7 in the spec are recorded with context B1.
